actors.viewer: Community member watching a live stream
actors.app: UIKit frontend (overlay, controls, pause/Reconnecting/ended indicators) — iOS / Android / RN / Flutter / WebUIKit
actors.player: Playback engine (AVPlayer on iOS / HLS.js on web) — seek-to-live-edge, buffering, reconnect/auto-retry
actors.sdk: Amity SDK — Room status (live / ended / recorded / waitingReconnect) + the real-time chat subscription
actors.network: Device network layer between the app and the broadcast/SDK

flows.name: Default — playing at live edge before any pause
flows.summary: Baseline: a Live stream plays at the live edge with the chat running live and no pause indicator, before the viewer interacts.

steps.action: watches a live stream (Room status = live) at the live edge and has not yet paused
reports Room status = live and keeps the real-time chat subscription active
plays continuously at the live edge
shows no pause indicator (the ▶ overlay is absent) and renders the LIVE badge / viewer count as-is — unaffected by this feature
pushes new chat messages in real time; the chat displays live because nothing is paused

unit: render Live player at the live edge (Room status = live) → assert NO pause indicator (▶ overlay) present
assert LIVE badge and viewer count render as-is (feature does not alter them)
mock the SDK chat subscription → assert new messages render live while nothing is paused (BR-14)
scenario: open a live stream and do not pause → verify playing at the live edge, no ▶ overlay, chat updating live
e2e: {iOS, Android, web-desktop}: load a live broadcast, assert no pause indicator and live chat streaming before any interaction

flows.name: Pause a live stream
flows.summary: Viewer pauses a Live stream → the ▶ overlay IS the pause indicator, chat keeps running live, tapping outside dismisses the control with no seek and the stream stays paused.

steps.action: (mobile: iOS/Android) taps to reveal the controls overlay then taps the central pause button — 2 steps; (web-desktop) taps directly to pause — 1 step
pauses live playback on the explicit user pause
shows the central play (▶) button overlay AS the pause indicator — no separate badge or banner
the chat subscription keeps running independently of playback — new messages continue to arrive and display in real time; chat is NOT paused
leaves the LIVE badge / viewer count as-is (updating them is out of scope for this feature)
taps anywhere outside the play button
dismisses the overlay control (pause/play button only — a Live stream exposes no ±10s seek controls); no seek occurs
remains paused after the tap-outside — dismissing the overlay does not resume playback

unit: mobile {iOS, Android}: assert 2-step pause — reveal controls, then central pause button pauses (BR-09 / PV-1)
web-desktop: assert 1-step pause — a single tap pauses directly (BR-09 / PV-1)
on pause → assert the central play (▶) overlay IS the pause indicator; assert NO separate badge/banner element (BR-07)
assert the Live player exposes NO ±10s seek controls — only pause/play (BR-01)
mock chat during the pause → assert chat keeps receiving and displaying new messages (separate subscription, not paused — BR-14)
tap outside the play button → assert overlay dismisses AND player stays paused, no seek (BR-11)
scenario: iOS: reveal controls → tap pause → verify ▶ indicator, chat still live, LIVE badge unchanged; tap outside → overlay gone, still paused
web-desktop: single-tap pause → tap outside → verify overlay dismissed and stream still paused
e2e: per-platform matrix {iOS, Android, web-desktop}: pause a live broadcast, assert ▶ indicator + live chat continuing + tap-outside dismiss keeps the stream paused
web-mobile is EXCLUDED — it cannot pause a Live stream at all (BR-02, see flow-UC2-F08)

flows.name: Resume → current live edge (not the paused position)
flows.summary: Viewer resumes → the player snaps to the CURRENT live edge (a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE vs today's resume-from-paused-position), landing within buffering tolerance, with chat uninterrupted.

assumptions.text: Resume-to-live uses 'a few seconds behind live' buffering tolerance as the accepted resume target; tighter is not achievable (live-streaming physics). Awaiting PM confirmation — non-blocking, CONF-07 already accepts 'expected'.

steps.action: taps the play button to resume the paused live stream
seeks to the CURRENT live edge (iOS seekToLiveEdge()+play()) and resumes — NOT from the previous paused position
a brief buffering/loading may occur while catching up to live; lands within normal buffering tolerance — a few seconds behind live is expected, not exact-live
dismisses the pause indicator (▶ overlay) as playback resumes
the chat subscription was never interrupted by the pause — no messages are missed or replayed; chat is already at the live moment

unit: on resume → assert the player seeks to the current live edge, NOT the paused position (BR-13)
assert the resume target ≈ live WITHIN buffering tolerance — a few seconds behind live is EXPECTED; do NOT assert exact-live (CONF-07)
assert the pause indicator (▶ overlay) dismisses on resume
iOS: assert the seekToLiveEdge()+play() path fires (LiveStreamPlayerView.swift:27-50)
mock chat across pause→resume → assert no messages replayed or skipped (BR-14)
scenario: pause ~15s then resume → verify playback jumps to the live moment (not where it was paused), within tolerance, chat uninterrupted
e2e: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE — run on every supported platform {iOS, Android, web-desktop}: pause then resume, assert playback lands ≈ live within tolerance (NOT exact, NOT paused position), chat continuous

flows.name: Long pause → resume still snaps to the live edge
flows.summary: After a multi-minute pause, resume snaps to the current live moment regardless of how large the jump is; a brief buffering state is acceptable while it completes.

steps.action: pauses a live stream and leaves it paused for an extended period (minutes)
stays paused throughout the extended period — no auto-resume
Room remains live and the chat subscription keeps running through the long pause (independent of playback)
taps play to resume after minutes away
snaps to the current live edge regardless of how far behind it is — the size of the jump does not change the guarantee
shows a brief buffering/loading state while the large jump completes, then lands within live buffering tolerance
dismisses the pause indicator (▶ overlay) on resume

unit: pause for minutes then resume → assert the player snaps to the current live edge regardless of jump size (BR-13)
assert a brief buffering/loading state is acceptable while the large jump completes
assert resume NEVER returns to the paused position, no matter the pause duration
scenario: pause 2 min vs 10 min → verify both resume to the live moment within tolerance; the larger jump may buffer briefly
e2e: {iOS, Android, web-desktop}: long pause (minutes) then resume, assert live-edge snap + brief buffering acceptable, still ≈ live within tolerance (not exact)
if the Room ends during the long pause, that is flow-UC2-F06 (ended/recorded wins), not this flow

flows.name: Chat / video re-sync on resume
flows.summary: Chat is a separate real-time subscription that never paused; on resume the video snaps to live and aligns with chat — no messages are replayed or skipped.

steps.action: has a live stream paused for a while; chat kept running live throughout the pause
the real-time chat subscription is INDEPENDENT of playback — it kept receiving and displaying new messages the whole time the video was paused; chat is never buffered or replayed to match the video
taps play to resume
snaps the video to the current live moment (per AC-02 / flow-UC2-F03)
chat continues uninterrupted at the live moment — no messages are replayed (re-shown) and none are skipped, because the chat was never paused
the video and chat are now aligned at the live moment; the transition is smooth and a brief buffering is acceptable

unit: assert chat is a SEPARATE real-time SDK subscription, independent of AVPlayer/HLS.js play state (BR-14) — model chat steps distinctly from player steps
capture the chat message list before/after resume → assert NO message is replayed (re-shown) and NONE is skipped
on resume → assert the video snaps to the live moment while chat is already at live → they align
scenario: pause with chat active → post messages during the pause → resume → verify those messages were shown live during the pause and none re-appear on resume
e2e: {iOS, Android, web-desktop}: drive chat traffic during a paused window, resume, assert chat continuity (no replay/skip) and smooth video/chat alignment at the live moment

flows.name: Stream ends while paused → ended/recorded wins
flows.summary: Room transitions to ended/recorded during the pause → the terminal state ALWAYS overrides paused, no frozen frame; if the recording is not ready the player shows 'Livestream ended' with no 'processing' state.

steps.action: has a live stream paused (player state = paused)
the broadcast / room lifecycle ends server-side; the recording may or may not be ready yet
pushes the Room status change from live to a terminal state (ended, or recorded once processed)
leaves the paused state and moves to the ended/recorded state — the terminal room state always wins over paused, even if the pause and the end occur simultaneously
shows the appropriate ended or recorded state — the viewer is not left on a frozen frame with no feedback
if the recording is not yet ready, shows 'Livestream ended' — there is NO intermediate 'processing' state

unit: while player state = paused, flip SDK room.status live→ended → assert the player leaves paused and shows the ended state (terminal state wins, BR-12)
assert ended/recorded takes priority EVEN IF the pause and the end occur simultaneously (BR-12)
recording not yet ready → assert 'Livestream ended' is shown, with NO intermediate 'processing' state (BR-12)
assert the viewer is never left on a frozen frame with no feedback (BR-15)
scenario: host ends the broadcast while the viewer is paused → verify the viewer transitions to ended/recorded, not stuck on the paused frame
e2e: {iOS, Android, web-desktop}: pause the viewer, end the broadcast server-side (SDK room.status→ended), assert the ended state overrides paused; recording-not-ready shows 'Livestream ended' (no 'processing')
distinct from flow-UC2-F07 (network drop): here the ROOM ended (SDK terminal state) and the stream does not resume

flows.name: Network drops while paused → Reconnecting, stays paused, resume→live
flows.summary: The network drops while paused → a 'Reconnecting' auto-retry indicator surfaces (platform-specific), the stream STAYS paused (no auto-resume), and on user resume it snaps to the live edge.

steps.action: has a live stream paused (player state = paused)
the device network connection drops

shows a 'Reconnecting' indicator with auto-retry (no manual retry button) — the viewer is not left on a no-feedback frozen frame. iOS: tied to device network (NWPathMonitor), shows EVEN while paused. Web: gated on a playback stall, so generally NOT shown while paused
auto-retries the connection in the background (web: HLS.js startLoad()/recoverMediaError()) but does NOT change play state — the stream stays paused, no auto-resume

state_change.state: paused — unchanged (no implicit toggle on a network stall, BR-10)

steps.action: the connection recovers
dismisses the 'Reconnecting' indicator; the stream is still paused (no auto-resume)
taps play to resume
snaps to the current live edge (iOS seekToLiveEdge()+play()) — not the paused position (per AC-02), landing ≈ live within tolerance

unit: iOS: the reconnecting overlay is tied to DEVICE network via NWPathMonitor → assert it shows EVEN while paused (LiveStreamViewerView.swift:244-272, NetworkMonitor.swift:11-28)

web: the 'Reconnecting' overlay is gated isLoading && isPoorConnection && isLive and fires on a playback STALL ('waiting') → assert it generally does NOT show while paused (a paused <video> emits no 'waiting'); it appears only if the SDK flips room.status='waitingReconnect' (LivestreamOverlay.tsx:57-66, LivestreamPlayer.tsx:128)
assert the stream STAYS paused through drop→recover — NO auto-resume (BR-10: play state changes only via explicit user play or a terminal room state)
assert reconnect is auto-retry with NO manual retry button (BR-15)
on user resume after recover → assert snap to the live edge, ≈ live within tolerance not exact (per AC-02); iOS seekToLiveEdge()+play() (LiveStreamPlayerView.swift:27-50)
scenario: iOS: pause → drop device network → verify the 'Reconnecting' scrim shows despite being paused; recover → still paused; tap play → live edge

web: pause → drop network → verify NO 'Reconnecting' overlay (no stall while paused); recover → tap play → live edge. Separately: SDK room.status='waitingReconnect' (host/broadcaster dropped) → the overlay DOES show
e2e: iOS: toggle device network while paused → assert overlay shows + stays paused + resume→live
web: route/network interception while paused → assert no stall overlay; then simulate room.status='waitingReconnect' → assert overlay shows; on recover + resume → assert snap to live edge
distinguish the viewer's device-network overlay from room.status='waitingReconnect' (the host/broadcaster lost connection, SDK-side)

renders and plays the Live stream

assert this is a standing platform boundary (platform table 68264), not a defect — nothing to file
